newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo, London club say some progress in debt talks.
newsitem.headline: Yugo, London club say some progress in debt talks.

text.p: Yugoslavia and its commercial bank creditors made some progress in debt-rescheduling talks and would meet again at the end of August, according to an official press release on Friday.

"Progress has been made on the economic assumptions determining the ability to pay that will be used for future negotiations which will take place at the end of August," the government and the banks said in a joint statement.
No details were available in the statement, issued after two days of talks between the government and co-chairs and economists of the International Co-ordination Committee of commercial banks.

"It is very important that the contact is maintained through working talks on a very high level. This is a positive signal that we shall resolve this important issue in a working and constructive atmosphere," Yugoslavia's Deputy Prime Minister Nikola Sainovic earlier told a news conference. He made no further comment.
Belgrade asked in mid-June for an 80 percent write-off of its outstanding $2.4 billion debt to commercial banks and restructuring of the remaining $481 million via a 25-year syndicated loan facility.
Bankers said the request was unacceptable and suggested a 50-60 percent debt write-off would be more realistic.
The proposal came as a surprise to markets during June talks in London.
Yugoslavia insists its debt-rescheduling proposal is based on a realistic capacity of its economy to meet obligations towards its creditors.

The London club delegation, including representatives from Chase Manhattan, Societe Generale and Westdeutsche Landesbank, was provided with additional data on Yugoslavia's balance of payments, cash flow projections and other essential financial forecasts.
Those completed the economic package initially presented in London by Yugoslavia's delegation, the press release said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4254
